facts: Three brothers who had quarrelled with the complainant over a drain waited for him outside the temple. Two of them caught hold of his arms while the third struck him on the head with an iron rod. The medical report records a fracture of the skull. All three ran away together.

charges.title: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means
charges.reason: The accused voluntarily caused hurt to the complainant using an iron rod, which is an instrument likely to cause death.

charges.title: Punishment for rioting
charges.reason: Three brothers acted together with a common object of hurting the complainant, constituting a riot punishable under this section.
charges.doubt: an unlawful assembly needs five or more persons; the facts show 3

charges.title: Punishment for murder
charges.reason: The use of an iron rod to strike the head causing a skull fracture indicates an intention or knowledge that death might be caused, engaging the offence of murder by attempt.
charges.doubt: The facts show a fracture of the skull but do not establish that the act was done with the intention to cause death or that death actually occurred.

charges.title: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon
charges.reason: The riot was committed while armed with a deadly weapon (iron rod), attracting enhanced punishment under this section.
charges.doubt: an unlawful assembly needs five or more persons; the facts show 3

charges.title: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention -
charges.reason: All three brothers acted in furtherance of the common intention to hurt the complainant, making them jointly liable.

sections.title: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means
Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention -

defenses.argument: The prosecution has failed to prove that the iron rod used was an instrument 'likely to cause death' as required by Section 324. The facts merely state a fracture of the skull, which is a grievous hurt but does not establish the specific intent or objective likelihood of causing death necessary for this aggravated charge.
defenses.fact_quote: The medical report records a fracture of the skull

defenses.argument: Section 147 requires an 'unlawful assembly' consisting of five or more persons acting in common. The facts explicitly state that only three brothers were present and involved in the incident, which falls short of the statutory minimum for a riot.

The charge of murder requires proof of the intention to cause death or knowledge that death would be a probable consequence. The facts only record a fracture of the skull, which constitutes grievous hurt but does not establish the specific intent (mens rea) required for murder.
defenses.fact_quote: The medical report records a fracture of the skull

defenses.argument: Similar to Section 147, the elements of 'riot' and 'unlawful assembly' are not met because the facts show only three persons involved. The presence of a deadly weapon (iron rod) is irrelevant if the requisite number of persons for an unlawful assembly is absent.

facts_profile.why: The facts disclose a criminal assault involving violence and injury caused by an unlawful assembly acting on a common object.
